```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This page lists every setting in harnessr: the core's first, then the
document layer's, stage by stage, and last the building blocks the document
settings choose between. harnessr builds the tables from `gr_settings_table()`
and the registries when the page is built, so they match the installed code.

A setting with a walkthrough links to it. The walkthrough is a section of a
guide that covers what the setting trades off, the signs that you should
change it, where its default came from and how to test a change.

```{r message = FALSE}
library(harnessr)
old <- hr_options(verbose = FALSE, embedder = "lexical")
settings <- gr_settings_table()
core <- c("options", "evaluate")
stages <- unique(settings$stage)
stages <- c(intersect(core, stages), setdiff(stages, core))
table(settings$stage, settings$tier)[stages, ]
```

## Reading the tables

Each row is one setting, and these columns describe it:

- `where`: the function that takes the setting.
- `default`: the value used when you give none. A string appears without
  quotes, a set of choices shows its first choice, and anything else appears
  as R code.
- `tier`: `basic` for the few settings most runs change, `advanced` for the
  rest.
- `status`: where the default came from. `measured` means a measurement backs
  it, `cited` means a published source gives it, and `untested` means it was
  chosen and nothing has measured it. A blank means nothing is declared, as
  for switches, limits and most function arguments.

`gr_settings_table()` also returns the `source` behind each status. For the
full help, see `?gr_read_spec`, `?gr_segment_spec`, `?gr_ingest_spec` and
`?hr_options`.

You give a setting where its stage takes it. You set options for the session
with `hr_options()`, and evaluation settings are arguments of their functions.
Ingest, segment and read settings go in a spec (`gr_read_spec(top_k = 4)`), in
a recipe, or by name to `answer_document()`, `gr_read_many()` and `gr_arm()`,
which put each on the step it belongs to. Review settings are arguments of
their functions.

To find out whether a value works better on your documents, build one arm per
value with `hr_sweep()` and compare the arms with `hr_benchmark()` and
`hr_report()`, as `vignette("compare")` does. `hr_sweep_check()` reports
which values sent the same requests.

```{r}
show_settings <- function(stage) {
  s <- settings[settings$stage == stage, ]
  esc <- function(x) gsub("|", "\\|", ifelse(is.na(x), "", x), fixed = TRUE)
  # Descriptions are Markdown: a bare "<field>" would reach the page as an
  # HTML tag and vanish. A < inside backticks would show as "&lt;", so keep
  # it out of code spans.
  lt <- function(x) gsub("<", "&lt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  name <- ifelse(is.na(s$guide), paste0("`", s$name, "`"),
                 sprintf("[`%s`](%s.html#%s)", s$name, sub("#.*", "", s$guide),
                         sub(".*#", "", s$guide)))
  knitr::kable(data.frame(setting = name, where = paste0("`", s$where, "`"),
                          default = paste0("`", esc(s$default), "`"),
                          tier = s$tier, status = esc(s$status),
                          description = lt(esc(s$description))),
               row.names = FALSE)
}
```

## Core settings

These settings belong to the core: the session options every call reads, and
the arguments of the functions that measure configurations.

### Options

Session settings. You set them with `hr_options()`, and a run reads them when
it starts. Most apply to every call, with or without a document; a few, such
as `cache_documents` and `embedder`, serve the document layer. Each core guide
covers its own: the model, endpoint, retries and actor in `vignette("core")`,
prices and the token counter in `vignette("models")`, the safety margin and
the reply's reserve in `vignette("context")`, the reasoning floor in
`vignette("effort")`, and the limits in `vignette("runs")`.

```{r echo = FALSE}
show_settings("options")
```

### Evaluation

The arguments of `hr_benchmark()`, `hr_report()`, `hr_judge()`,
`gr_compare()`, `hr_error_correlation()` and `hr_step_command()`.
`vignette("evaluate")` and `vignette("compare")` cover them, and "A governor
for one run" in `vignette("runs")` covers the `governor` a benchmark is held
to. `gr_compare()` belongs to the document layer and is listed here with the
other comparisons.

```{r echo = FALSE}
show_settings("evaluate")
```

## Document settings

The document layer's settings, in the order a run meets its stages. A
document run also reads the core options above: its requests are calls like
any other, under the same model, limits and token counter.

### Ingest

These settings control what comes out of a file: cleaning, OCR, the PDF
layout pass, and the floor on how much text must survive. The entries of
`cleaner_opts` and `layout_opts` appear under their parent's name, as
`cleaner_opts.references_after`. `vignette("ingest")` covers them.

```{r echo = FALSE}
show_settings("ingest")
```

### Segment

harnessr cuts the text into chunks with these settings. `vignette("segment")`
covers them.

```{r echo = FALSE}
show_settings("segment")
```

### Read

With these settings you choose how the model reads the chunks. The stage
also holds the ones `gr_read_many()` adds for a folder. `vignette("readers")`
covers them. `effort`, `effort_mode` and `context_policy` hand a read the
core's effort and context rules, which `vignette("effort")` and
`vignette("context")` explain.

```{r echo = FALSE}
show_settings("read")
```

### Screening

The arguments of these functions, which `vignette("review")` covers:

- `gr_screen()`, which decides which documents a review reads.
- `gr_reference()` and `gr_calibrate()`, which measure the screening against a
  person.
- `gr_screen_sample_size()` and `gr_stop_test()`, the sample size and stopping
  tests.

```{r echo = FALSE}
show_settings("screen")
```

### Extraction

The arguments of `gr_extract()`. The recipe settings you pass to it in `...`
are the ingest and segment settings above.

```{r echo = FALSE}
show_settings("extract")
```

### Synthesis

The arguments of `gr_claims()`, `gr_outline()`, `gr_gaps()` and
`gr_synthesise()`.

```{r echo = FALSE}
show_settings("synthesise")
```

## Building blocks

Some document settings choose a module from a registry: `extractor`, `clean`,
`method`, `reader`, `hr_options(embedder = )`, and the recipe you give
`answer_document()`. The tables below show the registries as installed, so a
module you register with `gr_register_reader()` or another `gr_register_*()`
function (`vignette("extending")`) appears in them too.

### Extractors

An extractor turns one kind of file into text. harnessr picks it by the
file's extension unless you name one with `extractor`.

```{r}
knitr::kable(gr_extractors()[, c("name", "extensions", "needs", "description")])
```

### Cleaners and presets

A cleaner removes one kind of noise from the text. Cleaners marked
`default_on` run unless the preset or list you give leaves them out. `early`
cleaners run before `late` ones, whatever order you name them in.

```{r}
knitr::kable(gr_cleaners()[, c("name", "stage", "default_on", "description")])
```

A preset is a named list of cleaners. This table shows the steps each preset
runs, read from what it did to the example report:

```{r}
presets <- c("none", "minimal", "standard", "academic", "scan", "legacy")
knitr::kable(data.frame(preset = presets, cleaners = vapply(presets, function(p) {
  steps <- names(gr_ingest(gr_example(), gr_ingest_spec(clean = p))$stats$clean_log)
  if (length(steps)) paste(steps, collapse = ", ") else "(none)"
}, character(1)), row.names = NULL))
```

### Segmenters

A segmenter decides where chunks are cut. `cost` says what it spends:
`free`, `embedding` for one embedding pass, or `llm` for model requests.

```{r}
knitr::kable(gr_segmenters()[, c("name", "cost", "needs_client", "description")])
```

### Readers

A reader decides how the chunks reach the model. `signature` records which
chunks it sends, how many requests it makes, and how information passes
between them. `cost_calls` is the number of requests.

```{r}
knitr::kable(gr_readers()[, c("name", "signature", "cost_calls", "description")])
```

### Embedders

An embedder turns text into vectors for the `retrieve` and `iterative`
readers and the `semantic` segmenter. A deterministic embedder gives the same
vectors every run, which a replay needs.

```{r}
knitr::kable(gr_embedders()[, c("name", "deterministic", "description")])
```

### Recipes

A recipe names an ingestion, a segmentation and a reader, with their
settings. The table shows the values each built-in recipe sets, and you can
override any of them by name.

```{r}
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, lapply(names(gr_recipes()), function(n) {
  r <- gr_recipes(n)
  data.frame(recipe = n, clean = paste(r$ingest$clean, collapse = ", "),
             method = r$segment$method, max_tokens = r$segment$max_tokens,
             overlap_tokens = r$segment$overlap_tokens, reader = r$read$reader,
             top_k = r$read$top_k)
})))
```

```{r include = FALSE}
hr_options(old)
```
